vendorApp.description: Vendor application id: a lowercase kebab-case slug naming the legacy product, e.g. "coreone". Independent of the tenant.

appVersion.description: The version string the app reports, e.g. "CoreOne 7.4".

app.description: Which vendor application this profile describes.

variant.description: Tenant/variant id: a lowercase kebab-case slug naming one institution's deployment of a vendor app, e.g. "tenant-a". Tenants of the same app can differ in labels and layout (R7.2).

origin.description: Where the app is served: a URL origin such as "http://127.0.0.1:4010", or an environment token such as "${MOCKBANK_ORIGIN}" expanded by the loader. Artifact routes are resolved against it.

loginRoute.description: Route that shows the sign-on screen, e.g. "/".

credentialRef.description: Name of a credential held outside the artifact (resolved at run time from the environment/secret store), e.g. "mockbank-operator". It is a reference, never the secret itself.

conditions.description: Default outcome rules for every capability of this app. An artifact rule with the same code overrides the default. Scope must be "any_step": a profile has no steps.

code.description: Condition code logged when the dialog is handled, e.g. "known_dialog".

description.description: What the dialog is and why it is safe to handle it this way.

text.description: Text the native dialog message contains (normalized substring), e.g. "Scheduled maintenance".

items.description: A native dialog the app is known to raise at unpredictable points. Replay handles it as a recoverable condition (a dialog_text signature with a dismiss_dialog recovery); any other dialog is a failure.

knownDialogs.description: Native dialogs this app is known to raise that replay may handle.

description: Per-app, per-tenant configuration read by the compiler and replay: where the app lives, how to sign on, and how its runtime conditions look. Holds a credential reference, never a secret.

code.description: Outcome/condition code: snake_case, e.g. "member_not_found". Stable; calling agents branch on it.

class.description: How a recognised condition is handled. business_outcome: a valid answer returned to the caller (e.g. member_not_found), never a failure. recoverable: handled inside the run by a bounded recovery and logged, never returned. failure: the run stops with evidence (or escalates to a human).

description.description: What the condition means for the caller and the reviewer (R2.7).

text.description: Text that appears on the screen when the condition holds, e.g. "No records match your search criteria".

frame.description: Frame to look in; omitted = any frame.

oneOf.description: The condition shows a fixed message somewhere on the screen.

title.description: Text the document/window title contains, e.g. "Server Error".

frame.description: Frame whose document title is checked; omitted = the top document or any frame document.

oneOf.description: The condition replaces the page, recognisable by its title.

route.description: Glob over the route relative to the app origin, e.g. "**/login*". On a desktop surface: the screen id.

oneOf.description: The app has moved to a known route (e.g. back to the sign-on page).

text.description: Text the native dialog (alert/confirm/prompt) message contains, e.g. "Scheduled maintenance".

oneOf.description: A native dialog with a known message is open.
The last document load (top document or frame) returned a status in the range, e.g. 500–599 for a failed load. Surfaces without HTTP report the equivalent load failure.

signatures.description: Leaf signatures; the condition holds when at least one matches. any_of cannot be nested.

oneOf.description: Any of several signals identifies the condition (e.g. a title OR a body text).

signature.description: How a runtime condition is recognised from an observation, discriminated on `kind`. Evaluated deterministically by replay; no model is involved.

anyOf.description: The rule is checked before and after every step.

items.description: Step id: "s<NN>-<slug>", e.g. "s03-click-search". Assigned once by the compiler and kept stable when steps are edited or inserted, so evidence, drift reports and outcome-rule scopes keep pointing at the same step.

anyOf.description: The rule is checked only around these steps (e.g. not-found only after the Search click).

message.description: Element whose text becomes the result message. The text passes the redaction layer before it reaches any sink; omitted = the description is used.

recovery.description: Required when class is recoverable; forbidden otherwise.

oneOf.description: Close the recognised native dialog, then continue the current step.

target.description: The control that closes the interstitial, e.g. a "Continue" link.

oneOf.description: Click past an HTML interstitial (notice page, banner), then re-verify the current step.

max.description: Maximum number of retries of the current step. Always bounded.

backoffMs.description: Delay before each retry, in milliseconds.

oneOf.description: Re-run the current step (e.g. after a failed load). Never used for an irreversible step.
Sign on again: re-run the login-phase steps once, then the main steps up to the current one. Refused (session_lost) if an irreversible step already ran.

OutcomeRule.description: Recognises one runtime condition and says how it is classified and handled. Resolution order at replay: artifact rule, then app profile default, then engine catalog default.

oneOf.description: Preferred hop. Legacy framesets address frames by name (target="content"), so the name is part of the app wiring and survives layout and URL changes.

glob.description: Glob over the frame document URL path, e.g. "**/member/*.jsp".

oneOf.description: Fallback hop for unnamed frames: matches the frame by the path of the document it shows.

title.description: The frame `title` attribute or its document title.

oneOf.description: Fallback hop when neither name nor URL is stable.

items.description: One step down the frame tree.

FrameScope.description: Ordered frame path from the top document to the document that holds the target; [] means the top document. On a non-web surface this names the window/pane path instead.

description.description: Human-readable name of the target, e.g. "Search button in the member search form". Shown to operators and in failure reports.

ladder.description: Locator rungs in stability order (most stable first). The resolver tries each in turn inside `frame`; resolving on a later rung succeeds but is reported as drift.

TargetRef.description: A UI element the artifact acts on or checks, independent of any one selector technology.

exact.description: true: the name must match exactly. Omitted/false: case-insensitive substring.

rationale.description: Why this rung identifies the target robustly (R2.3): which stable property it relies on and what change would break it.

surface.description: Surface-tagged extras. Informational: the resolver never uses them as a primary rung, so the core rung stays expressible on a desktop surface (R7.1).

cssHint.description: A CSS selector recorded for diagnostics and drift reports only.

oneOf.description: Most stable rung: role + accessible name from the accessibility tree, which desktop UI automation trees also expose.

text.description: The label text associated with a form control.

surface.description: Surface-tagged extras. Informational: the resolver never uses them as a primary rung, so the core rung stays expressible on a desktop surface (R7.1).

cssHint.description: A CSS selector recorded for diagnostics and drift reports only.

oneOf.description: A form control found by its associated label.

text.description: The visible text of the element.

match.description: exact: whole normalized text; contains: substring.

rationale.description: Why this rung identifies the target robustly (R2.3): which stable property it relies on and what change would break it.

surface.description: Surface-tagged extras. Informational: the resolver never uses them as a primary rung, so the core rung stays expressible on a desktop surface (R7.1).

cssHint.description: A CSS selector recorded for diagnostics and drift reports only.

oneOf.description: An element found by its visible text.

headerText.description: Text of the header/label cell used as the anchor.

direction.description: Where the target cell sits relative to the anchor cell.

offset.description: How many cells away from the anchor (1 = adjacent).

oneOf.description: The cell beside or below a labelled cell. Robust for nested layout tables where values have no ids or labels.

labelText.description: Text in the row that labels the control.

control.description: The kind of control in that row.

oneOf.description: The control in the table/form row whose label cell has the given text (unlabelled legacy forms).

containerText.description: Text inside the nearest container (form/table) to scope to; omitted = the whole frame document.

index.description: 0-based position among matching elements in the container.

oneOf.description: LAST RESORT and BRITTLE: breaks whenever an element is added or reordered. Use only when no semantic rung exists; replay reports drift when it is the rung that resolved.

anchor.description: How the target is found relative to page structure.

rationale.description: Why this rung identifies the target robustly (R2.3): which stable property it relies on and what change would break it.

surface.description: Surface-tagged extras. Informational: the resolver never uses them as a primary rung, so the core rung stays expressible on a desktop surface (R7.1).

cssHint.description: A CSS selector recorded for diagnostics and drift reports only.

oneOf.description: An element found by its position relative to stable text in the page structure.

LocatorRung.description: One rung of the locator ladder. Rungs are tried in order and the first unique match wins. A visual-anchor rung (image/OCR match) is a design-only extension for non-DOM surfaces and is not part of v1.
